author: Associated Press
description:
Kalshi announces ‘mutual decision’ as Democrats say they plan to investigate Trump family’s investments

Donald Trump Jr is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi, the prediction market company said Thursday.

Kalshi described it as a mutual business decision between the two parties that followed a decision by Trump Jr’s investment firm, 1789 Capital, to increase its investment in Kalshi’s biggest competitor Polymarket.

Continue reading...
title: Donald Trump Jr exits as paid adviser for prediction market Kalshi

author: Lex McMenamin
description:
Protesters with the Sunrise Movement youth climate group push for new Senate leadership and ending the filibuster

Dozens of protesters with the Sunrise Movement, a youth climate organization, were arrested after staging a sit-in inside Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer’s Washington DC office Thursday

According to the Sunrise Movement, 54 people were arrested, among a few hundred who joined the protest from across the country, including some from New York, which Schumer represents. On its Instagram, the group is fundraising $24,000 to cover the bail fees and any potential legal fees for those arrested.

Continue reading...
title: Dozens of protesters arrested after staging sit-in at Chuck Schumer’s DC office

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Home Office sign-off also needed for site that would house 1,200 asylum seekers near Oxfordshire village that voted to leave UK

The communities secretary, Angela Rayner, has approved full planning permission for an asylum centre at a Ministry of Defence site near the village of Piddington in Oxfordshire.

The decision approves plans to go ahead with the refurbishment and redevelopment of the former barracks. The Home Office insists that final approval is still to be determined.

Continue reading...
title: Angela Rayner grants planning approval for asylum centre in Piddington despite local opposition

author: Jennifer Rankin in Dublin, Jessica Elgot, Lisa O’Carroll and Pippa Crerar
description:
Prime minister says reset could be a deal ‘like the Brexit people thought they were voting for in 2016’

Andy Burnham has said he believes a “win-win” deal could be done with the EU that could be “more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for in 2016”.

The prime minister was meeting fellow leaders at the European Political Community summit in Dublin, ahead of a keenly anticipated EU-UK summit next week, where he hopes to bring Britain closer to Europe.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Win-win’ deal with EU could be done, Andy Burnham says

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Kayla Smith stabbed Chloe Watson Dransfield to death during planned fight over young man

An 18-year-old woman who stabbed a teenage girl to death during a planned fight over a young man has pleaded guilty to murder.

Chloe Watson Dransfield, 16, was attacked by Kayla Smith, 18, after going to the latter’s home with her boyfriend Blake Dowling in Leeds, West Yorkshire, a court heard.

Continue reading...
title: Woman, 18, admits murdering girl, 16, in Leeds

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Figures highlight spread of virus, officially declared eliminated in US in 2000, but CDC does not identify which states accounted for deaths

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported six measles-related deaths in the US this year, according to figures published on its website on Thursday, as the country faces its most severe resurgence of the disease in decades.

The newly reported total is twice the number of deaths recorded in 2025, highlighting the spread of the highly infectious virus, which was officially declared eliminated in the US in 2000.

Continue reading...
title: CDC reports six measles deaths in 2026 as US battles worst outbreak in 35 years

author: Auzzy Byrdsell in New York
description:
New York City officials have confirmed at least eight casualties – six adults and two children – in the collapse

Flatbush Ave in Flatbush, New York, stood still and in shock after a three-story apartment building collapsed on Wednesday afternoon near a construction site.

“The last time I saw something like this was when I went to work at 9/11,” Prudence Foster said.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Who will be held accountable?’: fatal Brooklyn building collapse devastates community

author: Andrew Roth in Washington
description:
President says vice-president will focus on supposed ‘Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States’

  • US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump has said that the US is no longer seeking a deal to end the war with Iran and ordered JD Vance, who had spearheaded recent efforts to restart negotiations with Iran, to focus on domestic politics instead.

In a post to his social media site on Thursday, Trump said he was redirecting the vice-president to focus his “complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S”.

Continue reading...
title: Trump orders JD Vance to stop Iran war negotiations and focus on domestic policy

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
Donalds is governor-elect in state that leads the US in the number of executions, with its 20th this year taking place next week

Three exonerated former death row prisoners in Florida have called on incoming governor Byron Donalds to halt the state’s record run of executions and review the cases of all 235 prisoners who are now condemned.

At a press conference in Tallahassee on Thursday hosted by the advocacy group Floridians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty (FADP), the men said they were seeking a roundtable discussion with Donalds, a Republican, as well as the state’s new legislative leaders in pursuit of a moratorium.

Continue reading...
title: Former death row prisoners call Byron Donalds to halt future Florida executions

author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
description:
‘I must now listen to my body and my doctors’, says Taylor, who was one of the earliest members of the new wave hit-makers

The drummer for Duran Duran, Roger Taylor, is to step down from the band due to worsening tinnitus.

In a statement, Taylor said: “This is one of the hardest decisions I’ve ever had to make. Playing drums in this band has been the joy of my life, and I’ll never be able to properly thank the fans for the love they’ve shown us over the years. But the truth is that my tinnitus has been getting steadily worse, and I’ve reached the point where I must now listen to my body and my doctors.”

Continue reading...
title: Duran Duran drummer Roger Taylor leaves band due to tinnitus

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with George Chidi; produced by Angus Neale; senior producer Leonore Schick; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description:
Mississippi has elected the Democrat Scott Colom in a historic race in the traditionally deep-red state, making him its first Black senator since shortly after the US civil war. The closely contested race was called more than a week after the US midterms, with Colom running against the Republican incumbent, Cindy Hyde-Smith. How did Colom’s grassroots campaign win despite limited early backing from national Democrats? Lucy Hough speaks to politics and democracy reporter George Chidi – watch on YouTube

Continue reading...
title: Mississippi makes history with Democrat senate win - The Latest

author: Pjotr Sauer and Jennifer Rankin in Dublin
description:
Hardline remarks come as Ukrainian military faces disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service

Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.

During the talks at the Kremlin with the US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.

Continue reading...
title: Putin says Russia would target foreign troops deployed to Ukraine

author: Associated Press
description:
• Russians ‘have no business’ in country, says minister

  • Skating and cross-country skiing first to be affected

Finland says it will restrict entry to the country for Russian athletes because of the war in Ukraine, potentially affecting a number of winter sports. The move follows a backlash in Finland to Russia being reinstated for the ice hockey world championships.

“As long as Russia’s war of aggression continues, Russian athletes have no business in Finland,” said Elina Valtonen, the Minister for Foreign Affairs. “Their entry into the country would be a threat to Finland’s international relations. The same is true of other short-term work under visas that is not essential to Finland’s national interests.”

Continue reading...
title: Finland bars Russian athletes from entering country over Ukraine war

author: Jessica Elgot
description:
Exclusive: Former health secretary says he wants to ‘tear up the old approach’, with under-25s to lose personal independence payments

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Some young people with disabilities will lose their personal independence payments and will have to apply instead to a local fund for short-term expenses and equipment, Alan Milburn’s review will recommend.

While those with the most severe needs’ entitlement will be protected, others will be asked to apply for money for specific purposes rather than an ongoing payment.

Continue reading...
title: Local fund to replace Pip for some young disabled people under Milburn plans

author: Kirsty McEwen
description:
Police are looking for suspect after incident at Logan Circle, one mile north of the White House

  • Multiple people shot in Washington DC as police warn people to stay inside

Multiple people have been shot in north-west Washington DC on Thursday morning, local police confirmed have confirmed, prompting a “barricade situation” in the area.

In a statement at 9.21am ET, the DC police said that the incident has “resulted in a barricade situation in the 1500 block of 15th Street, Northwest”.

Continue reading...
title: Washington DC shooting latest updates: multiple people shot in Logan Circle

author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
description:
Just 28.2% of 18- and 19-year-olds have received their first dose in one-off campaign, UKHSA says

The clock is ticking for young people in the UK to receive vaccinations to protect against meningitis B, experts have said, as figures reveal fewer than one in three eligible in one-off campaign have received their first dose.

Earlier this year an unprecedented outbreak of meningitis B in Kent and clusters of cases in Dorset and Berkshire caused three deaths, as well as life-long health consequences among some of those who survived.
title: Time running out for young people to receive meningitis B vaccines in UK

author: Ariel Bogle
description:
Young people are being found with ‘hard drives full of what can only be described as gore’, one expert says

In March, Guardian Australia revealed that most people who have been charged with the new federal crime of possession of violent extremist material are under 18.

This week Australian federal police sounded the alarm about a surge in teen extremism: 32 of the 37 young people prosecuted in counter-terrorism cases since 2020 were charged in the past two years.

Continue reading...
title: What’s behind Australia’s surge in teen extremism?

author: Anne Davies
description:
Chris Minns is trying to address the threat of undeclared lobbying but falls well short of what the commission recommended five years ago

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

A dirt file on a state minister peddled to journalists. A subterranean campaign to discredit the building commissioner. Convincing the Liberal party to unseat councillors in the Hills district who were blocking a developer.

The New South Wales corruption watch
title: Icac’s drama and dirt files show NSW’s ‘guns for hire’ problem. But neither major party is serious about reform

author: Penry Buckley, Josh Butler and Bertin Huynh
description:
Expert warns of ‘huge loophole in political communication laws’ as state government among parties presenting accounts as unaffiliated news sources

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

“Breaking,” a reel from the Instagram account nswnewsroom reads. “Another Liberal MP quits, almost a third now gone.”

The post looks like it could have been made by a media outlet. It cites the source as the Daily Telegraph and Jordan Lane, a New South Wales MP, who is the sixth sitting Liberal member to announce they won’t re-contest their seat at the March 2027 election.
title: NSW’s latest news Instagram account has an unlikely group behind it: the Labor party

author: Sarah Butler
description:
US investment firm Gordon Brothers is ‘taking due care’ to consider if one of three bidders has enough funds

  • Business live – latest updates

Poundland’s owner has said it is “taking due care” to consider if one of three bidders had enough funds to ensure its survival after the troubled budget retail chain secured two more weeks to find a deal.

The management of Poundland, which employs approximately 12,000 people and operates 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, won approval from the high court for an extension of legal protection from creditors on Thursday morning.

Continue reading...
title: Poundland owner secures two extra weeks to ensure retail chain’s survival

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Shares up 7% after announcement as Jaime Gilinski Bacal seeks exit three years after helping to rescue bank

Metro Bank is putting itself up for sale three years after its near-collapse, in a move that could hand a £420m windfall to its Colombian billionaire investor, Jaime Gilinski Bacal.

Metro Bank made the rare decision to publicly announce it was open to bids on Thursday, paving the way for a wider pool of suitors. The announcement pushed the share price up by 7% by mid-morning, valuing the bank at about £1.3bn.

Continue reading...
title: Metro Bank up for sale, with billionaire investor in line for £420m windfall

author: Taz Ali
description:
Colom adds to blue wave of Democrat victories across the US and becomes Mississippi’s first black senator since 1875 after defeating Cindy Hyde-Smith

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email

Hello, and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Mississippi has elected Scott Colom, a Democrat, as its senator, adding to a wave of Democratic gains across the country in this year’s midterm elections.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I had the courage to believe in Mississippi’ says Scott Colom after historic Senate win – US politics live

author: Caroline Davies and agency
description:
Former Radio 1 DJ accused of new offences against women in London and now faces trial in January for 17 charges

The former radio DJ Tim Westwood has denied two additional sex offences dating back to 1991 and 2004.

His latest not guilty pleas mean he now denies 17 charges against nine women between 1983 and 2016.

Continue reading...
title: Tim Westwood in court to deny two more sexual offence charges

author: Andrew Sparrow (now) and Taz Ali (earlier)
description:
Milburn’s review is considering how to address the growing number of young people classified as not in education, employment or training

Good morning. I’m Andrew Sparrow, taking over from Taz Ali.

Andy Burnham won’t arrive in Dublin for his meeting with other leaders from the European Political Community (the EU plus non-EU states in Europe) until this afternoon, but it is the first time he has met many of them, and they are anticipating his arrival.

So the negotiations will not be that easy, but I think we can take the little steps. And I’m confident that if we are together, we are much stronger when it comes to economy, but when it also comes to security.

Continue reading...
title: Young people should get fewer welfare benefits, according to Milburn review on the workforce – UK politics live

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Rallies take place on more than US 40 campuses as workers seeking better pay and conditions decry stalled talks

Starbucks baristas, students, elected officials and allies are holding rallies at over 40 college campuses across the US on Thursday to support the Starbucks Workers United boycott campaign as the union nears five years of deadlock with the company over contract negotiations.

Starbucks Workers United is seeking better pay and stronger staffing levels, including a $17 an hour minimum wage for baristas and a minimum staffing of three wo
title: College students rally in support of Starbucks baristas urging boycott over contract impasse

author: Oliver Milman in Antalya
description:
Kerry decries president for ceding clean-energy dominance to China and says climate crisis still a key issue for voters

Donald Trump is the “biggest loser we’ve seen in a long time” for scrapping action on the climate crisis and ceding the clean energy race to China, former US secretary of state John Kerry has said.

Kerry, speaking at the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey, criticized Trump for withdrawing the US from the international climate process and axing measures that reduced planet-heating emissions. Unlike almost all other countries in the world, the Trump administration has sent no delegation to the resort city of Antalya for the annual UN climate talks, which started on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: Trump the ‘biggest loser’ for scrapping climate action, John Kerry says at Cop31

author: Robert Booth and Denis Campbell
description:
Exclusive: The Guardian revealed 29 hospital trusts were not or hardly using the controversial patient data tech

NHS England has deleted a claim from its website stating 137 hospital trusts are benefiting from Palantir’s AI health data system after the Guardian revealed 29 of them were not using all or most of the controversial technology.

Health bosses had published a list of all the NHS bodies “live” with and “realising benefits” from the AI-powered federated data platform (FDP), a system set up to improve patient outcomes, boost operating theatre efficiency and speed up bed discharges. But after 29 trusts said it was either not live or they were not using any of its applications, the original list of hospitals appears to have been taken down.
title: NHS England deletes ‘misleading’ claim 137 trusts benefiting from Palantir AI tools

author: Press Association
description:
Thomas changes plea over slashing boat with knife after watching occupants being helped by rescue services

The far-right activist Daniel Thomas has admitted criminal damage after slashing an inflatable dinghy with a knife in the Channel.

The 37-year-old, who is known as Danny Tommo, changed his plea to the single charge when he appeared via video link from prison at Portsmouth crown court on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Far-right activist Daniel Thomas admits criminal damage of dinghy in the Channel

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
Britain’s national wealth fund invests £113m in UForce, whose equipment has been used heavily in war with Russia

A London-based naval drone maker founded by Ukrainians has reached a £4.5bn valuation after it raised more than £500m from investors including the UK government.

UForce, which makes military drones for land, air and sea, received £113m from the UK’s national wealth fund. The investment makes UForce one of the UK’s fastest-growing unicorns – or startups with a valuation of more than $1bn. Its drones have been used extensively in the war in Ukraine.

Continue reading...
title: UK drone maker founded by Ukrainians hits £4.5bn value after raising £500m

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are attempting to make further progress after earlier talks in Abu Dhabi

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are in Moscow this morning, where they are expected to meet Russia’s president Vladimir Putin to advance some of the issues discussed at trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi over the last two days.

The meeting is expected to get under way around 9am GMT, with Russia’s deputy foreign minister Sergei Rybakov trying to manage everyone’s expectations by saying it was too early to say that necessary trust had been restored between Russia and Ukraine.

Continue reading...
title: US envoys expected to meet Putin in Moscow to discuss Ukraine ceasefire - Europe live

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
Regulator to hasten review over concerns that firms are ‘undermining’ rules to make large payments to bosses

The water company bonus ban is set to be tightened after the regulator accused the industry of a risk of “damaging public trust” with large payments to bosses that appeared to get around the rules.

Anglian Water was singled out for particular criticism over “retention payments” worth up to £800,000 for chief executive Mark Thurston despite the bonus ban. Anglian will face increased monitoring of its governance arrangements because of the controversial payments.

Continue reading...
title: Water industry bonus ban to be tightened as Ofwat warns of ‘damage to public trust’

author: Phillip Inman
description:
ONS also says GDP rose 0.2% month on month in September, in a boost to the chancellor, John Healey

The UK economy grew by 0.7% in the third quarter, as expected by City analysts, confirming that consumers and businesses remained resilient despite high oil and gas prices.

The Office for National Statistics said a jump in the cost of petrol, diesel and natural gas prices following the re-escalation of the conflict in the Middle East played an important role in restricting economic growth in the three months to the end of September.

Continue reading...
title: UK economy grows by 0.7% in third quarter despite high oil prices

author: Josh Butler
description:
Workplace relations minister Amanda Rishworth launches best practice guide on AI adoption after Qantas and Canva job cuts

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Entry-level jobs will be the first to be automated due to AI, but it could mean fewer hours and higher wages for ordinary workers – or make jobs tougher with more burnout and workplace surveillance – the government has warned employers.

While major companies like Qantas and Canva slash their workforces in restructures spurred by AI changes, work
title: Fewer hours and higher wages – or more burnout and surveillance: employers told to prepare for AI

author: Hettie O'Brien
description:
In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang

Good morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies.

Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines.

UK | Ministers are considering
title: Thursday briefing: What we do (and don’t) know about Alice Huang and the Nvidia affair

author: Caitlin Cassidy and Luca Ittimani
description:
‘You just don’t mess or play with a 400-tonne train’, Sydney Trains says as 17-year-old suffers multiple injuries to head, chest and pelvis

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A 17-year-old boy is in a critical condition after falling from the outside of a train on the Sydney Harbour Bridge while he was likely train surfing, NSW police say.

Around 11.30am on Thursday, emergency services were called to the railway corridor between Wynyard and Milsons Point train stations following reports someone had fallen from a northbound Tangara train onto the tracks on the bridge.
title: Teenager in critical condition after likely ‘train surfing’ on Sydney Harbour Bridge, police say

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
Exclusive: Former barrister who helped legally establish that secondhand smoke causes lung cancer argues states could seek up to $50bn in compensation

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian state governments could sue tobacco companies for billions in public hospital and healthcare costs, under a proposal developed by a former barrister who helped legally establish that secondhand smoke causes lung cancer.

The South Australian government is formally seeking advice on the proposal, while other states are reviewing it.

Continue reading...
title: Australian states could sue tobacco companies for billions in healthcare costs under proposal

author: Kat Wong
description:
Court hears former police officer agrees he was trying to destroy evidence that might incriminate him

Beau Lamarre-Condon has admitted he threw Jesse Baird’s phone off a bridge to destroy evidence after allegedly murdering him, a court has heard.

The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon admits throwing Jesse Baird’s phone off a bridge after alleged murders, trial hears

author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
description:
Inspectors find some officers acted on potential matches from retrospective searches without making enough checks

Police officers risk arresting innocent people, especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found.

Although the technology can help fight crime, the report found it is beset by errors and biases, and operators do not always realise they must make further inquiries to verify the data.

Continue reading...
title: Facial recognition errors put ethnic minorities at risk of wrongful arrest, police watchdog warns
